name: SeaGuard — read me first
info:
SeaGuard: safety and boundary alerting for small fishing boats.

Deploy this flow and everything starts by itself in live mode.
Open the dashboard at /dashboard and go to the Test lab tab to run a randomized test campaign.

Requirements (Manage palette → Install):
  @flowfuse/node-red-dashboard, node-red-contrib-aedes, node-red-contrib-web-worldmap

Settings live in the Config node next to this comment: base URL, Telegram bot token,
harbour position, boundary, thresholds. Coordinates are illustrative, not navigational.

name: Config
The simulated world and the boat firmware
info:
Physics produces one raw sensor reading per boat per simulated second.
The firmware node is the code that would run on the boat: it debounces the sensors,
sends telemetry and confirmed emergency events over LoRa, keeps a 1 Hz trip log and
uploads it over harbour Wi-Fi.

name: Boat firmware (edge)
Physics and sensors
Harbour Wi-Fi link
Edge diagnostics log
Radio channel and shore gateway
info:
The LoRa channel model applies loss, duplicates, delay and blackouts, then the gateway
forwards packets onto MQTT. An injected gateway outage really disconnects this MQTT client,
so the shore sees the last-will message and the gateway buffers what it cannot send.

Shore server
info:
Everything that runs in the control room: MQTT ingest with sequence tracking and
acknowledgements, geofencing, the weather service, the correlation engine and the
alert notifier. The three mock endpoints at the bottom stand in for the harbour
Wi-Fi API, Open-Meteo and Telegram during test runs.

Clock, campaign generator and oracle
info:
The clock turns real time into simulated seconds. The controller builds a randomized
campaign from a seed, injects each fault at its scheduled second, and plays the part of a
duty officer who acknowledges some alerts and ignores others. The oracle then checks what
the system did against what each fault should have caused.

One publisher builds a view model per page once a second, so the user interface never
sees the raw tick rate. Buttons in the pages send commands back through the router.
